script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

Title: FRESH STARTS

INT. APARTMENT LIVING ROOM - DAY

JOHN (40s, anxious, overweight), sits on the couch, staring at his laptop. His girlfriend, MARY (30s, elegant, confident), walks in.

MARY
(smiling)
Hey, John. What's got you so focused today?

JOHN
I can't take it anymore. I've decided to start my own business.

MARY
(laughs)
That's great, John! When did you become an entrepreneur?

JOHN
I've had this idea for a while now. A food delivery service that only uses electric bikes. No cars. No emissions. I'll call it "GreenRide."

MARY
(smiling)
That's wonderful, John. I believe in you.

Suddenly, JIM (30s, cocky, charming), a former business partner and friend, bursts in.

JIM
(grinning)
Hey, John! I heard you're starting your own business. That's a risky move, buddy.

JOHN
(defensive)
Mary and I are excited about it. It's time for a fresh start.

Jim chuckles and shakes his head.

JIM
A fresh start? After everything we've been through? I'm not so sure about that, John.

INT. APARTMENT KITCHEN - NIGHT

John, Mary, and Jim sit around the kitchen table, discussing business matters. The conversation turns heated, and Jim brings up old grievances.

JIM
You remember that deal we had in Brazil? The one with the shady supplier? You cost me thousands, John.

John looks down, ashamed.

JOHN
I'm sorry, Jim. That was a mistake. I've learned from it.

JIM
(laughs)
Learned from it? You expect me to just forget about it?

Mary steps in.

MARY
(calmly)
Gentlemen, let's focus on the present. John's new business could be a great opportunity for both of you.

Jim glances at Mary, considering her words.

JIM
Fine. I'll give it a chance. But only because of you, Mary.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

John and Jim sit across from each other, discussing the GreenRide business plan. Jim's attitude softens as they work together, and they begin to rebuild their friendship.

EXT. GREENRIDE WAREHOUSE - DAY

John, Mary, and Jim stand together, watching as a team of workers assemble electric bikes. The GreenRide logo is proudly displayed on the wall behind them.

JOHN
(smiling)
We did it, guys. This is just the beginning.

Mary and Jim share knowing looks, understanding the importance of forgiveness and fresh starts.

MARY
(smiling)
I believe in us.

JIM
(smiling)
I'm with you, John.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.
